item.title: Huawei convicted of stealing trade secrets: What’s the case, and what does it mean for US-China ties? Explained
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co., China’s largest technology company, was found guilty of 10 of 12 US criminal charges, including that it defrauded banks about its business in Iran and money laundering.
item.dc:creator: Livemint
item.content:encoded: A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies Co. of stealing trade secrets Tuesday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.Huawei Technologies Co., China’s largest technology company, was found guilty of multiple US criminal charges, including that it defrauded banks about its business in Iran and money laundering, Bloomberg reported.A federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, deliberated for about four days before reaching a verdict Tuesday in a rare US prosecution of a foreign corporation.What are the US charges against Huawei?Jurors found Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) reported.The company was cleared of two charges, including racketeering and obstruction of justice, the report added."No person or company is above the law," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft,” he added.The equipment manufacturer was accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process, news agency AFP reported.That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment."The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology," the DOJ said in a release.Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed.The investigation also involved Huawei's business dealings with the government of Iran."Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community," DOJ said.The jury ultimately acquitted the company of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice."Today's verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead," Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva said in a statement.Huawei now faces potential fines, forfeiture and restitution but the US has not specified the scope of financial penalties it will seek.Trump admin accuses Huawei of ‘spying’The world's leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei has been targeted by the Trump administration, which alleges a risk of it spying on behalf of the Chinese government.The United States has previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.For most of that time, the company has been largely excluded from the American market under trade measures imposed by the Trump and Biden administrations in the name of national security, Bloomberg reported.The telecom titan has emerged as China’s de facto national chipmaking champion and is one of a handful of firms central to Beijing’s goal of dominating artificial intelligence and replacing American software and circuitry with local equivalents.What the verdict means for US-China ties?The verdict against one of China’s biggest and best-known tech giants lands at a delicate time for US-China relations. According to Bloomberg, it threatens to strain ties already frayed over revelations that the now-reinstated chief executive of Nvidia Corp., Jensen Huang, had an affair with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence.Besides, the conviction is a vindication for the Justice Department, which overcame attempts by Huawei to derail the case before trial and had to navigate years of delays because of the Covid pandemic, which made it difficult for lawyers and witnesses to travel.Along the way, two Chinese intelligence officers were accused in 2022 of trying to bribe a US law enforcement official with $61,000 in Bitcoin to steal evidence and get inside information about the case.From the beginning, the Huawei case heightened tensions between Washington and Beijing while the world’s two largest economies were mired in a trade war.Months later, officials in Donald Trump’s administration labeled the company a national security threat, alleging that it sold telecommunications equipment that could be used by China’s Communist Party for spying.The initial criminal indictment set off a diplomatic crisis when Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou, whose father founded the company, was arrested at the behest of the US on financial fraud charges while traveling through Canada. Almost three years after Meng was held under house arrest in Vancouver, she reached a deferred prosecution agreement in 2021 that allowed her to return to China, but after she admitted that the company violated US sanctions by illegally conducting business in Iran.(With inputs from Bloomberg, AFP)

item.title: Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Check fuel cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
item.description: Global oil prices steadied as traders balanced indications of rising global supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported.
item.dc:creator: Livemint
item.content:encoded: Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Petrol and diesel prices have remained largely steady across major cities despite a surge in global crude oil costs due to the US-Iran war, which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri attributed this to the Centre's strategy of cutting excise duties and managing domestic fuel supplies. Here is a look at the petrol and diesel prices in major metropolitan cities as of November 25: New Delhi: Petrol is retailing at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel is priced at ₹95.20 per litre. The national capital continues to have relatively lower fuel prices compared to other metros. Mumbai: In the financial capital, petrol is priced at ₹111.21 per litre, and diesel costs ₹97.83 per litre. Chennai: Residents in Chennai are paying ₹107.76 per litre for petrol and ₹99.55 per litre for diesel. Kolkata: Petrol costs ₹113.51 per litre, while diesel costs ₹99.82 per litre. Bengaluru: Petrol is priced at ₹110.44 per litre, and diesel at ₹99.56 per litre. Hyderabad: Petrol costs ₹116.15 per litre, while diesel costs ₹104.23 per litre. Petrol and diesel prices in other metro cities today Source: GoodReturns Oil steady after gain Oil prices steadied as traders balanced indications of rising global supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported. Brent crude traded around $91 a barrel after climbing 2.3% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) hovered below $82. On Tuesday, Iran claimed a fourth tanker was struck by a mine, according to the Fars news agency, extending a recent wave of vessel attacks by the Islamic Republic. Tehran also warned it would tighten its grip over the Strait of Hormuz until its demands are met, Tasnim reported—highlighting that an end to the nearly nine-month conflict remains out of reach. Even so, crude shipments from the Persian Gulf have surged in recent months, prompting the International Energy Agency (IEA) to forecast that the market will tip into a surplus this quarter. “The reality on the ground is more a ‘war but no war’ situation, with spasms of violence,” Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC, told Bloomberg. Under that scenario, “look for the supply surplus to become the dominant theme in coming weeks,” he added. Brent has dropped sharply this month as Gulf exports climbed and US President Donald Trump held off on renewed strikes against Iran following the US midterm elections. Adding to the downward pressure, a key timespread for the Middle East’s Dubai crude benchmark flipped into a bearish structure this week, signalling that supply is now outpacing demand, Bloomberg noted.

item.title: RFK Jr. Calendars Show Meetings With Lilly, Chipotle CEOs
item.description: The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what HHS called a push for greater transparency.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what HHS called a push for greater transparency.The documents span agencies across the health department and include records previously released under the Freedom of Information Act and other public documents, HHS said in a news release. The department will update the site as more documents are made public.About a quarter of the documents on the new site have not been previously made public, a spokesperson for HHS said.Though Kennedy has been a frequent and vocal critic of corporate influence in medicine and agriculture, his calendars show many meetings with business leaders in healthcare, food and other industries.The calendars list a meeting with Eli Lilly & Co. Chief Executive Dave Ricks in April 2025, a pull-aside during a visit to Indiana when he also met with Governor Mike Braun. A separate entry for February 2026 shows a meeting with Novo Nordisk A/S. A May 2026 entry shows a call with George Yancopoulos of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc.A meeting with the CEO of Tylenol-maker Kenvue Inc. preceded the administration’s White House news conference in which President Donald Trump told pregnant women to avoid the painkiller, citing unproven theories of a link to autism. The meeting occurred three days after the Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration was expected to link the drug to autism.Other entries show meetings with CEOs of infant formula makers, a roundtable with hospital executives and a session with insurance CEOs.Kennedy, who has also criticized the food industry, met in March 2025 with Donnie King, CEO of Tyson Foods Inc. at the time. He has also met with leaders from Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc., Starbucks Corp, and In-N-Out Burgers.Kennedy also met Stacey Kennedy, the US CEO of tobacco company Philip Morris International Inc., the listings show.A June 2026 entry shows a meeting with SoftBank Group Chairman Masayoshi Son along with Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.Kennedy has had regular meetings with Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, a key vote for his confirmation.Three CenturiesThe documents appear to range from as early as 1840 (a handwritten catalog of the surgeon general’s library) through the first half of 2026. More than 10,000 records were from previous centuries, according to search results returned by the site.The site is searchable and offers some initial “collections,” prominently featuring a batch of documents on Covid-19. Other collections include records on infant formula, the opioid crisis and several batches related to FOIA litigation.Kennedy’s calendars show meetings with other cabinet officials and media appearances, including briefings on the ongoing measles outbreak starting in February 2025, when cases were increasing in Texas. HHS said it’s also using artificial intelligence to process public records requests and propose redactions for trade secrets or other information subject to withholding. Thousands of documents have been requested under FOIA and the use of AI will allow quicker searches and reviews, the agency said.The transparency website replaces an online reading room that previously aggregated records released under FOIA and other documents.Last year, the Department of Government Efficiency led by Elon Musk cut thousands of staff across HHS, including in the FOIA departments, impairing the agency’s ability to respond to records requests quickly.The Food and Drug Administration has previously published the agency’s response letters for new drug and biologic applications.--With assistance from Ike Swetlitz, Allison DeAngelis, Daniela Sirtori, Redd Brown, Jeff Kao and Ilena Peng.(Updates with additional details starting in fourth paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
